name: CT-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: DeLauro's long incumbency and seniority in a D+8 district
No competitive polling or expert ratings signal vulnerability
model.rationale: DeLauro combines a D+8 seat, decades of incumbency, and a roughly 75-to-1 fundraising advantage over Chris Lancia, while prediction markets price her at 96%. Nothing in the evidence suggests more than a token Republican challenge.
model.watch: A major outside-spending intervention or an unexpected incumbent scandal would be the only plausible route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rosa DeLauro seeks another term in a Connecticut district that leans Democratic by about eight points, and she enters with the advantages of long incumbency and seniority. Her challenger, Chris Lancia, has raised only about $15,000, while DeLauro has raised more than $1.1 million and holds a large cash cushion, with essentially no outside money opposing her.

Prediction markets give DeLauro roughly a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters or public polls flag the race as competitive. A third-party candidate, Thomas Egan, is on the ballot but shows no measurable support or funding. The fundamentals, money, and market pricing all point the same direction, making this a Safe Democratic seat with only modest residual uncertainty.
